Prompts: REA_17 §3.4. · edge (catalyst pole only; owner 2026-10-16, THE EDGE v9: two sentences, the energy and its three ruling domains from the GOD table, then a clause per domain in The Pattern's voice; the metric; the head derived in the app)

candidates.structural_interaction: Depth amplifying depth — perceptual intelligence running without form
candidates.k2_overview: Your Water moves as the Twin: a current that keeps its own channel while running beside others. You match people without merging into them, fluent in company, private in depth. Two rivers to the same sea is your model of friendship: shared direction, separate water, and no argument about whose current is whose.
candidates.k2_functional: Your energy runs in currents: even output for weeks, then a quiet season to refill the source.

k2_domain_readings.Peers: Your peers are parallel currents: fellow travelers heading the same direction by different beds. You collect companions across every landscape you cross. Keep a few for the whole length of the river, not just the pretty stretches.
k2_domain_readings.Independence: Water independence is having your own source: income, opinions, and inner weather that no one else controls upstream. Protect the headwaters. Everything else about you can flex.
k2_domain_readings.Self-reliance: You route around what others need rescuing from, so smoothly that nobody notices there was an obstacle. Occasionally say the obstacle out loud. Even self-sufficient rivers deserve witnesses.

catalyst.define: Running thin, the well is shallow. You draw from it with care, and little is spilt or shared.

angles.drive: Carrying your own weight is the first thing you do. Being a load on nobody feels like safety, and you carry what is yours rather than hand a corner to a peer. Nobody ever has to wonder whether you will do your share.
angles.cost_self: Carrying everything yourself is what steadies you most. Water runs short in you before the week does, and you keep each load rather than share it. All of the strain lands on your shoulders and nobody else's.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you carry the whole weight yourself, you leave the people beside you nothing to hold. You put the load ahead of the closeness sharing brings. Friends who would gladly help you stay on the outside of your hard weeks.

angles.drive: An even pace is how you get through everything. You carry little Water, so you keep one steady pace rather than match every start and stop around you. You arrive at the end of a long stretch with something left to give.
angles.cost_self: Your even pace holds you up through a long week. Little Water comes in, and you spend it steadily rather than in bursts. Chances that call for a sudden push slip by while you hold your stride.
angles.cost_others: Keeping an even pace leaves the people near you to match it or go on alone. You put your pace ahead of theirs, and a hurried friend walks a stretch alone. Anyone who drops back always finds you right where they left you.

angles.drive: Deciding alone is your default. Asking around feels like handing over what is yours, so you decide by yourself instead of a second view. Your choices come quick and clean, with nobody else's doubts mixed in.
angles.cost_self: Alone with a decision, you are at your most sure. You keep the choice yours rather than take a second opinion, the one place blind spots get named. The mistakes a friend would have caught are yours to pay for.
angles.cost_others: Each time you decide alone, you decide for the people it touches too. You settle it first, and a peer hears the plan instead of shaping it. The people closest to you live by choices they had no part in.

friction.define: Running over, the depth fills with no way out. Needing nobody feels safest to you, but the weight then builds up where no one can help carry it.

angles.drive: You keep to yourself even among people you like. Your own company is where you feel steady, and you share your days without sharing much of what is in them. Those who love you know your habits better than your heart.
angles.cost_self: Keeping to yourself spares you the work of explaining. You need your inner life to stay your own, and most of what you feel never gets said aloud. Underneath, you would like one person to know you well.
angles.cost_others: Keeping to yourself leaves the people close to you guessing at your mood. Privacy feels like solid ground to you, and your inner weather stays behind a quiet face. They are left to read you from small signs.

angles.drive: Never asking is a rule you keep and never say. Water piles up in you unshared, so you manage alone rather than ask a peer for an hour. You have taught everyone around you that you need nothing, and the lesson stuck.
angles.cost_self: Managing without asking is what you do best. Owing anyone feels worse to you than the work, and you choose doing it alone rather than asking for company. You miss out on the ease that help would have given you.
angles.cost_others: Each time you never ask, you take away a friend's chance to be useful. You keep the need to yourself rather than hand a peer one small job. You leave your peers at a distance, with nothing of yours to help with.

angles.drive: Expecting the same of everyone keeps your standard honest. You hold yourself to a hard line, and you hold your peers to it rather than to their own. You measure people by a rule they never agreed to, and few can match it for long.
angles.cost_self: Rarely let down, you hold everyone to the same standard. Water runs deep and stays hidden, and you would rather keep your own rule than lower it for company. You lose a lot of good company while waiting for the perfect match.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you expect the same from a peer, you hand them your standard without asking for theirs. You judge their effort by your own rather than by what they had to give. You hold back the credit their effort had already earned.

edge.lead: Water runs through your family, your growth and your social life. It is the same you who comes home on good days and bad, the choice you make alone and stand by either way, and the friends you choose when being alone already suited you.
